h1: The 7 Best Eufy Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Eufy Robot Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven Eufy robot vacuums from the E25 flagship to the 11S MAX, compared on suction, mopping, docks and low-furniture clearance.
summary: The eufy E25 is the best Eufy robot vacuum, combining 20,000 Pa suction with a HydroJet roller mop and a self-washing dock. The E28 Matic adds a portable tool for stairs and upholstery. The C28 is the value roller mop at 15,000 Pa, and the C10 and 11S MAX are the vacuum-only options.
intro: Eufy sells robots at two very different levels of effort: ones that wash their own mops and ones that just vacuum. The common mistake is buying a mop-capable model when your floors are mostly carpet, or buying a vacuum-only unit and wishing it mopped. Decide on the mop first, then choose the dock, because the dock is where most of the price and most of the upkeep live.

We reviewed seven Eufy models on paper, ranking them on stated suction, mop design, dock automation, profile height and price tier. The ranking leans on listings and owner reports, so treat the dock claims as manufacturer descriptions. Suction figures run from 15,000 to 20,000 Pa where stated, and four listings give no figure at all.

products.name: eufy E25 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 20,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: Top suction with a HydroJet roller mop and self-washing dock.
products.description:
The E25 lists 20,000 Pa suction, a HydroJet roller mop and a self-washing dock, as a vacuum and mop combo, at $500+. A roller mop presses a continuous wet pad against the floor while the dock rinses it, so the robot never drags dirty water across tile on the second pass. Pa is a manufacturer figure for suction pressure, and 20,000 sits at the top of this group.

It ranks first because it joins the highest suction tier to a mop that cleans itself. Next to the E28 Matic you trade the detachable carpet tool for a simpler, mop-first design, and next to the C28 you gain 5,000 Pa. It costs more than anything below it.

Buy it for a home with hard floors that wants strong suction and real mopping. The caveat is the $500+ price, and carpet-heavy homes will use little of the mop.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting top suction and real roller mopping.

products.name: eufy E28 Matic Robot Vacuum and Mop, 20,000 Pa, Portable Carpet Cleaning
products.verdict: A robot vacuum plus a detachable tool for stairs and upholstery.
products.description:
The E28 Matic also lists 20,000 Pa suction, with a Matic mop system, a self-maintaining dock and portable carpet cleaning, at $500+. The portable piece is the point: it gives you a handheld-style cleaner for stairs, upholstery and car interiors that a robot can never reach, so the dock does double duty.

It ranks second because that detachable tool covers areas the E25 cannot, but the mop system differs from the E25's HydroJet roller, and the listing gives less on how the mopping works. More parts also mean more to wash and store. The suction number ties the E25, so the call is accessory versus roller mop.

Choose it if you want a spot-cleaning tool along with the robot. The caveat is complexity: extra pieces to charge, clean and lose, plus the same $500+ price.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want to clean stairs and upholstery too.

products.name: eufy X10 Pro Omni Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, Dual Mops with 12mm Auto-Lift
products.verdict: Dual rotating mops that lift 12mm over carpet, with an Omni dock.
products.description:
The X10 Pro Omni has dual rotating mops with a 12mm auto-lift and an Omni all-in-one dock, as a vacuum and mop combo, in the $200 to $500 bracket. Auto-lift raises the mop pads off the floor when the robot meets carpet, so it can clean hardwood and rugs in one run without soaking the rug.

It ranks third because the listing gives no suction figure, while the E25 and E28 state 20,000 Pa and the C28 15,000. Its strength is the lift: 12mm clears low rugs, which suits pet homes where the robot crosses carpet and hardwood many times. The Omni dock also handles emptying and washing.

Buy it if you have pets and mixed floors. The caveat is the missing suction spec, so you cannot judge deep-carpet pickup, and the design is older than the roller models above it.
products.idealFor: Pet owners with carpet and hardwood.
products.skipIf: You want a published suction number.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 15,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: Roller-mop washing at 15,000 Pa without the flagship price.
products.description:
The C28 lists 15,000 Pa suction, a HydroJet roller mop and a self-washing dock, as a combo, in the $200 to $500 bracket. It carries the same mop concept as the E25 at a lower price tier, which is where the roller design makes the most sense for buyers who dislike scrubbing mop pads.

It ranks fourth because it steps down from the E25's 20,000 Pa but keeps the roller mop and self-washing dock. That makes it the better value among the roller models. Against the X10 Pro, it gains a stated suction number but loses the 12mm auto-lift.

Choose it for roller-mop washing on a lower budget. The caveat is the lower suction, which matters on carpet, and it lists no detachable tool for stairs.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting roller mopping on a budget.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo for Hardwood and Carpet
products.verdict: Omni dock convenience with a hardwood and carpet mode.
products.description:
The Omni C20 has an Omni all-in-one dock, a self-emptying design and a hardwood and carpet mode, as a vacuum and mop combo, in the $200 to $500 bracket. The Omni dock empties the dust bin so you handle the robot only for refills and filter cleaning.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives no suction number and few mop details, and it targets convenience rather than power. The X10 Pro lists 12mm auto-lift and dual rotating mops, which are specific features, while the C20 offers a mode and a dock. Without numbers, the C20 is harder to judge against the C28.

Buy it for a mixed-flooring home that wants dock automation. The caveat is the missing suction spec, and the vague mop description means you should read the listing before ordering.

products.name: eufy C10 Robot Vacuum Self Emptying, 8 Weeks Hands Free, 2.85-Inch Slim
products.verdict: A 2.85 inch slim vacuum that self-empties for up to 8 weeks.
products.description:
The C10 is a vacuum-only robot with a 2.85 inch slim profile and a self-emptying dock rated for 8 weeks hands free, in the $200 to $500 bracket. A low body slides under beds and sofas where thicker robots get stuck, and weeks between emptying cuts the most annoying chore.

It ranks sixth because it has no mop, which limits it against the combos above, and the listing gives no suction figure. It does fit under low furniture and keeps dock upkeep to a minimum. Compared with the 11S MAX, you gain self-emptying but pay a bracket more.

Choose it if you have decided you do not need mopping, or if you have carpet-heavy floors. The caveat is price: $200 to $500 for a vacuum-only unit is hard to justify unless the self-emptying matters.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a slim vacuum-only unit.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner, Super Thin, Quiet
products.verdict: The lowest price and simplest upkeep, with a super-slim quiet body.
products.description:
The 11S MAX is a vacuum-only robot with a super-slim profile and quiet operation, with no dock to maintain, in the $100 to $200 bracket. The simplicity is the appeal: no bags, no dock bin and no mop pads, so setup and upkeep are close to nothing. Quiet running suits homes where the robot runs while people work.

It ranks last because it has no mop and no self-emptying, so you empty the bin by hand. It is also the cheapest here, a full bracket under the C10. Without suction, mapping or mop figures, it competes mostly on price.

Buy it as a first robot vacuum or on a tight budget. The caveat is manual upkeep: expect to empty the bin often, and look elsewhere if you want mopping.

whatMatters.detail: Roller mops press and wash a continuous pad, while rotating mops spin two pads. A roller is the more thorough design on paper because the pad stays clean as it works. The E25 and C28 list a HydroJet roller, and the X10 Pro lists dual rotating mops. Look for the mop name in the title.

Docks may empty dust, wash mops or both. Self-washing saves you rinsing pads by hand, and self-emptying cuts bin chores to weeks apart. The Omni name usually signals an all-in-one dock. Check for self-washing, self-emptying or Omni on the listing, and note that docks need regular filter and tank cleaning, which no listing here describes in detail.

Pa is a suction pressure claim, and 15,000 to 20,000 Pa sits at the high end. It matters most on carpet, where dirt hides deep in the pile. Remember it is a manufacturer figure, and several Eufy listings here give none. Compare like with like, and do not treat a bigger number as a promise of performance.

A 2.85 inch body fits under many sofas and beds, so the robot can clean spaces other robots skip. Measure your lowest furniture clearance, including the bed frame, before you decide. Check the height in the listing bullets, and note that a mop-equipped combo is usually taller than a vacuum-only unit, so check both.

Auto-lift raises mop pads over carpet to avoid wetting it. The X10 Pro lists 12mm, enough for a low-pile rug but not for thick carpet. Check the figure on your listing, and measure the rug height. If you have carpet in most rooms, a vacuum-only unit avoids the issue altogether and costs less.

faq.q: Which Eufy is best for pets?
faq.a: The X10 Pro Omni is aimed at pet homes with carpet and hardwood. Its 12mm auto-lift handles carpet to hardwood transitions, and the Omni dock cuts the chore of emptying fur, though its listing gives no suction figure.
They buy a mop model for a carpeted home. Mopping adds little there, so a vacuum-only unit like the C10 may suit better, and costs far less than the E25, whose mop would sit idle.

faq.q: Is the E25 worth it over the C28?
faq.a: If you want 20,000 Pa over 15,000 Pa, yes. Both have the HydroJet roller mop and a self-washing dock, so the extra spend buys suction only. If your floors are mostly hard, the C28 saves a price tier and still washes its roller.

faq.q: How do I set up the dock?
faq.a: Place it against a wall with clear space around it. Follow the app to map your home, and check that the dock sits where the robot can reach it from every room without crossing a threshold.

faq.q: How do I maintain the dock?
faq.a: Empty or replace the dust bag and clean the mop pad. The C10 lists 8 weeks between emptying, but filters, brushes and the bin still need regular cleaning to hold suction.
No. The 11S MAX is vacuum-only with no dock to maintain, and you empty its bin by hand. If you want mopping, step up to the C28 or another combo with a self-washing dock, such as the E25.

finalTake: Buy the E25 if you want strong suction and real mopping, and the E28 Matic if stairs and upholstery matter too. The C28 delivers the roller mop for less money, and the X10 Pro suits pet homes with mixed floors. Skip mop models entirely if your floors are mostly carpet.
